subject: HEALTH
title: Health 3
description: Third-grade health education covering nutrition and physical activity, body systems and growth, feelings, friendship and conflict resolution, injury prevention and safety (fire, traffic, water, emergencies, online), safe medicine use and the harms of tobacco, vaping and alcohol, and personal and community health. Students practice skills such as reading food labels, goal setting, refusal skills and handwashing, and finish with a health promotion project.
framework: 2008 California Health Education Content Standards; 2019 CA Health Education Framework

standards.H-3.1.1.N: Identify the food groups and the importance of eating a variety of foods from each group.
standards.H-3.1.2.N: Describe the benefits of eating breakfast, healthy snacks and drinking water.
standards.H-3.1.3.N: Explain how physical activity contributes to good health.
standards.H-3.2.1.N: Explain how media and advertising influence food and activity choices.
standards.H-3.3.1.N: Use food labels and reliable sources to find nutrition information.
standards.H-3.5.1.N: Use a decision-making process to choose healthy foods and snacks.
standards.H-3.6.1.N: Set a short-term goal to improve eating or physical activity and track progress.
standards.H-3.7.1.N: Practice planning and preparing balanced meals and snacks.
standards.H-3.8.1.N: Encourage family and peers to make healthy food and activity choices.
standards.H-3.1.1.G: Describe the major body systems (skeletal, muscular, digestive, circulatory, respiratory, nervous) and their functions.
standards.H-3.1.2.G: Explain how the five senses work and how to protect them.
standards.H-3.1.3.G: Recognize that people grow and develop at different rates.
standards.H-3.3.1.G: Identify trusted adults and professionals who can answer questions about growth and the body.
standards.H-3.7.1.G: Practice behaviors that keep body systems healthy.
standards.H-3.1.1.S: Identify safety rules at home, at school and in the community (fire, water, bicycle, pedestrian, passenger).
standards.H-3.1.2.S: Describe emergency situations and how to get help, including calling 911.
standards.H-3.1.3.S: Distinguish between safe and unsafe situations and identify trusted adults to tell.
standards.H-3.1.4.S: Identify ways to stay safe online and with technology.
standards.H-3.4.1.S: Demonstrate refusal skills and how to ask for help in unsafe situations.
standards.H-3.5.1.S: Use a decision-making process to avoid injury.
standards.H-3.7.1.S: Practice safety behaviors (helmets, seat belts, fire escape plans).
standards.H-3.1.1.A: Distinguish between medicines and other drugs and describe safe medicine use.
standards.H-3.1.2.A: Describe the harmful effects of tobacco, vaping and secondhand smoke.
standards.H-3.1.3.A: Describe the effects of alcohol on the body and behavior.
standards.H-3.2.1.A: Identify influences such as media and peers on alcohol, tobacco and drug use.
standards.H-3.4.1.A: Demonstrate refusal skills to avoid alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.
standards.H-3.8.1.A: Encourage others to be tobacco-, alcohol- and drug-free.
standards.H-3.1.1.M: Identify feelings and healthy ways to express them.
standards.H-3.1.2.M: Describe characteristics of healthy friendships and respect for differences.
standards.H-3.1.3.M: Describe bullying and ways to respond to and report it.
standards.H-3.4.1.M: Demonstrate effective communication, listening and conflict-resolution skills.
standards.H-3.5.1.M: Use a decision-making process for social situations.
standards.H-3.6.1.M: Set a personal goal and identify steps and supports to reach it.
standards.H-3.7.1.M: Practice healthy ways to manage stress and strong emotions.
standards.H-3.1.1.P: Explain how germs spread and how to prevent communicable disease.
standards.H-3.1.2.P: Describe proper dental care and its importance.
standards.H-3.1.3.P: Explain the importance of sleep, sun protection and personal hygiene.
standards.H-3.1.4.P: Describe how the environment affects health and ways to protect it.
standards.H-3.3.1.P: Identify health care professionals and community health helpers.
standards.H-3.7.1.P: Practice personal hygiene and health habits.
standards.H-3.8.1.P: Promote a healthy school, home and community environment.

resources.name: KidsHealth – For Kids
resources.note: Free kid-level articles and videos on the body, feelings, safety and nutrition

resources.name: MyPlate Kids
resources.note: USDA MyPlate food group guidance, activity sheets and games

resources.name: Safe Kids Worldwide
resources.note: Safety tips on bikes, pedestrians, water, fire and car seats

resources.name: Mouth Healthy Kids (American Dental Association)
resources.note: Free brushing and flossing videos and dental health activities

units.title: Nutrition and Physical Activity
units.big_idea: A variety of foods and daily activity give our bodies the energy to learn, play and grow.

units.title: Growth and Development: Body Systems
units.big_idea: Body systems work together, and healthy habits keep them strong.

units.title: Mental, Emotional and Social Health
units.big_idea: Understanding feelings and communicating well help us build healthy relationships.

units.title: Injury Prevention and Safety
units.big_idea: Knowing safety rules and how to get help prevents injuries.

units.title: Medicines, Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drugs
units.big_idea: Medicines can help when used safely; tobacco, vaping and alcohol harm growing bodies.

units.title: Personal and Community Health
units.big_idea: Daily habits and a clean environment protect our health and our community's.

units.title: Health Promotion Project
units.big_idea: We can use what we know to help others be healthy.

objectives: Identify the five food groups
Explain why variety matters

days.title: Five food groups
days.work: Explore the MyPlate Kids page and name the 5 food groups with 3 examples each.

days.title: Food group sort
days.work: Cut pictures from grocery flyers and sort them onto a paper-plate MyPlate.

days.title: Nutrients
days.work: Learn one job of each nutrient (protein builds muscles, calcium builds bones) and match foods to jobs.

days.title: Food log
days.work: Record everything you eat for one day and tally servings from each group.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Identify which food group you ate least yesterday and name 2 foods to add.

objectives: Explain the benefits of breakfast, healthy snacks and water

days.title: Breakfast power
days.work: Discuss how breakfast fuels the brain and plan 3 balanced breakfasts with at least 3 food groups each.

days.title: Snack decisions
days.work: Use the decide-act-check steps to choose between snack pairs (chips vs. apple with peanut butter).

days.title: Water
days.work: Measure how many cups of water you drink in a day and compare to the recommended amount.

days.title: Sugary drinks
days.work: Measure the teaspoons of sugar in a can of soda using sugar and a teaspoon and compare to water.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a 'healthy snack menu' card for the kitchen with 6 choices.

objectives: Use food labels to compare foods

days.title: Label parts
days.work: Find serving size, calories, sugar, sodium and fiber on a Nutrition Facts label.

days.title: Compare cereals
days.work: Compare sugar and fiber in 3 cereals and rank them from healthiest to least healthy.

days.title: Ingredients
days.work: Read ingredient lists and learn that ingredients are listed from most to least.

days.title: Store hunt
days.work: At the grocery store, compare 2 brands of the same food and choose the healthier one with reasons.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer 5 questions about a new food label.

objectives: Explain how advertising influences food choices

days.title: Ad tricks
days.work: Analyze 2 cereal boxes for tricks (cartoon characters, prizes, bright colors).

days.title: Commercials
days.work: Watch 2 food commercials and identify who the target audience is and what they promise.

days.title: Healthy ad
days.work: Design an ad that makes a vegetable appealing.

days.title: Share
days.work: Present the ad and explain the techniques used.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write how ads might change what a kid wants to eat and how to think it through.

objectives: Explain how physical activity benefits the body
Set an activity goal

days.title: Benefits
days.work: List ways activity helps the heart, muscles, bones, mood and sleep.

days.title: Activity log
days.work: Log all physical activity minutes for a day and compare to the 60-minute goal.

days.title: Screen time
days.work: Track screen time and brainstorm active swaps.

days.title: Goal setting
days.work: Set a one-week SMART goal to add activity or a fruit/vegetable serving.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Check day 1 of the goal tracker and plan supports.

objectives: Plan and prepare a balanced meal
Encourage others to eat healthily

days.title: Meal plan
days.work: Plan a balanced dinner for your family using all 5 food groups.

days.title: Shopping list
days.work: Write a shopping list and estimate cost.

days.title: Cook
days.work: Help prepare the planned meal, practicing safe kitchen habits.

days.title: Family message
days.work: Make a poster encouraging your family to eat a rainbow of fruits and vegetables.

days.title: Unit 1 check
days.work: Review your goal tracker and take a quiz on food groups, labels and activity.

weeks.assessment: Unit 1 quiz; meal plan; goal tracker review

objectives: Describe the skeletal and muscular systems

days.title: Bones
days.work: Learn major bones (skull, ribs, spine, femur) and why bones need calcium.

days.title: Vinegar bone
days.work: Soak a cleaned chicken bone in vinegar to see what happens when calcium is removed; observe after 3 days.

days.title: Joints
days.work: Find hinge and ball-and-socket joints in your body and test their movements.

days.title: Muscles
days.work: Feel biceps and triceps work in pairs while lifting a book.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Label a skeleton and muscle diagram and list 2 ways to keep bones and muscles strong.

objectives: Describe how the digestive system works

days.title: Digestion path
days.work: Trace food from mouth to intestines on a diagram.

days.title: Stomach model
days.work: Mash crackers with water in a zip bag to model the stomach.

days.title: Intestine length
days.work: Measure a string as long as the small intestine (about 20 feet) and lay it out.

days.title: Fiber and water
days.work: Discuss how fiber and water help digestion.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write the digestion steps in order.

objectives: Describe the circulatory and respiratory systems

days.title: Heart
days.work: Learn the heart is a muscle that pumps blood; listen to a heartbeat through a paper towel tube.

days.title: Pulse
days.work: Measure pulse before and after exercise and graph results.

days.title: Lungs model
days.work: Build a balloon-lung model in a plastic bottle and demonstrate breathing.

days.title: Protect
days.work: List ways to protect the heart and lungs (exercise, no smoke).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain how the heart and lungs work together.

objectives: Describe the nervous system and five senses
Protect senses

days.title: Brain
days.work: Learn the brain's role as the control center and why helmets matter.

days.title: Reaction time
days.work: Do the ruler-drop reaction test 5 times and record results.

days.title: Senses test
days.work: Do a blindfolded taste and smell test.

days.title: Protect senses
days.work: List ways to protect eyes and ears (sunglasses, volume limits).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a senses chart with organ, job and protection.

objectives: Recognize people grow at different rates
Identify trusted adults

days.title: Growth
days.work: Compare baby photos to now and measure your height.

days.title: Different rates
days.work: Discuss why kids grow at different rates and that it is normal.

days.title: Trusted adults
days.work: List trusted adults and professionals to ask about body questions.

days.title: Doctor visit
days.work: Learn what happens at a check-up.

days.title: Unit 2 check
days.work: Complete a quiz on body systems and growth.

objectives: Identify feelings and healthy ways to express them

days.title: Feelings words
days.work: Build a feelings word bank of 20 emotions.

days.title: Body signals
days.work: Identify where you feel anger, worry and excitement in your body.

days.title: Expressing
days.work: Sort healthy and unhealthy ways to express anger.

days.title: Journal
days.work: Write a feelings journal entry about your day.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Role-play expressing a feeling using an I-message.

objectives: Practice healthy stress management strategies
Build a calm-down plan

days.title: What is stress
days.work: Discuss what stress feels like and list 5 things that cause you stress.

days.title: Breathing
days.work: Practice belly breathing and 5-finger breathing (trace your hand while breathing in and out) for 3 minutes.

days.title: Calm-down kit
days.work: Build a calm-down kit in a shoebox with a stress ball, drawing paper, a favorite book and breathing cards.

days.title: Move it out
days.work: Try 3 movement stress relievers (stretching, a brisk walk, a dance break) and rate how each felt.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a calm-down plan poster listing your 4 best strategies in order.

objectives: Describe qualities of good friends
Respect differences and show empathy
materials: friendship picture book (e.g., 'The Invisible Boy' by Trudy Ludwig, library)

days.title: Friend qualities
days.work: List 8 qualities of a good friend and rank your top 3.

days.title: Empathy
days.work: Read 'The Invisible Boy' (or similar) and discuss how Brian felt and what changed.

days.title: Differences
days.work: Interview a friend or relative about something different about them and something you share.

days.title: Inclusion
days.work: Plan 3 ways to include someone left out at a park, co-op or team practice.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a 'recipe for friendship' with ingredients and steps.

objectives: Demonstrate active listening, I-messages and conflict-resolution steps

days.title: Active listening
days.work: Practice active listening: partner tells a story, you repeat back the main points and a feeling.

days.title: I-messages
days.work: Write I-messages ('I feel ___ when ___ because ___') for 5 common conflicts.

days.title: Conflict steps
days.work: Learn 5 steps (cool down, talk, listen, brainstorm, agree) and make a pocket card.

days.title: Role-play
days.work: Role-play solving a sibling conflict over a shared toy using the steps.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain the conflict-resolution steps and when you would use them.

objectives: Describe bullying and ways to respond to and report it

days.title: What is bullying
days.work: Read the KidsHealth article on bullying and distinguish bullying (repeated, power imbalance) from ordinary conflict.

days.title: Types
days.work: Sort scenario cards into physical, verbal, social and cyberbullying.

days.title: Upstander
days.work: Practice 4 upstander responses (speak up, stay with the target, walk away together, get help).

days.title: Reporting
days.work: Practice telling a trusted adult the who, what, where and when of a bullying incident.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write and sign an upstander pledge.

objectives: Set a personal goal and identify steps and supports

days.title: Growth mindset
days.work: Turn 6 fixed-mindset statements ('I can't do this') into growth-mindset statements ('I can't do this yet').

days.title: Choose a goal
days.work: Set a personal goal (learn to ride without training wheels, read a chapter book, make a new friend).

days.title: Steps and supports
days.work: List 4 steps toward the goal and the people who can support you.

days.title: Track
days.work: Track progress on a 2-week calendar and note obstacles.

days.title: Unit 3 check
days.work: Complete a quiz on feelings, stress, friendship, conflict and bullying.

objectives: Identify fire safety rules
Make and practice a home escape plan

days.title: Fire rules
days.work: Learn rules about matches, lighters, stoves and space heaters, and find hazards in a home picture.

days.title: Smoke alarms
days.work: Test home smoke alarms with an adult and learn what the sound means.

days.title: Escape plan
days.work: Draw a home floor plan with two exits from every room and an outside meeting place.

days.title: Fire drill
days.work: Practice a home fire drill, crawling low under 'smoke' and timing how long it takes.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Demonstrate stop, drop and roll and explain your escape plan.

objectives: Practice safety rules for walking, biking and riding in vehicles

days.title: Pedestrian
days.work: Walk a neighborhood route with an adult practicing stop-look-listen and crosswalk rules.

days.title: Helmet fit
days.work: Fit your helmet using the eyes-ears-mouth test from Safe Kids.

days.title: Bike rules
days.work: Learn bike hand signals and ride a safe route, signaling turns.

days.title: Car safety
days.work: Learn California booster seat rules and the 5-step seat belt fit test.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a pedestrian, bike and passenger safety checklist.

objectives: Identify water, heat and sun safety rules
Make safe decisions outdoors

days.title: Water rules
days.work: Learn pool, lake and ocean safety rules, including what a rip current is and how to escape one.

days.title: Life jackets
days.work: Try on a life jacket and check it is the right size and fastened correctly.

days.title: Buddy system
days.work: Practice the buddy system and 'reach or throw, don't go' rescue rule.

days.title: Decisions
days.work: Use decide-act-check steps for 4 outdoor scenarios (thunderstorm at the beach, getting lost on a hike).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a water safety poster with 5 rules.

objectives: Describe emergencies and practice getting help

days.title: Emergency or not
days.work: Sort 12 situations into emergencies (call 911) and non-emergencies (tell an adult).

days.title: Calling 911
days.work: Practice a pretend 911 call stating your name, full address and what happened.

days.title: First aid
days.work: Learn basic first aid for small cuts, scrapes and nosebleeds and tour the home first aid kit.

days.title: Earthquake
days.work: Practice drop, cover and hold on in 3 rooms and identify safe spots.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make an emergency contact card with address, phone numbers and a trusted neighbor.

objectives: Distinguish safe and unsafe situations
Practice refusal and help-seeking

days.title: Safe vs. unsafe
days.work: Sort 10 scenario cards into safe, unsafe or 'check with an adult.'

days.title: Trusted adults
days.work: Draw a 'helping hand' tracing with 5 trusted adults, one on each finger.

days.title: Refusal skills
days.work: Practice 'say no, get away, tell someone' with firm voice and body language.

days.title: Body safety
days.work: Learn body safety rules: your body belongs to you and secrets about touching are never okay to keep.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Role-play 3 refusal scenarios with a parent.

objectives: Identify ways to stay safe online

days.title: Personal information
days.work: Sort information into okay to share online (favorite color) and private (address, school, photos).

days.title: Passwords
days.work: Create a strong passphrase and learn why passwords are shared only with parents.

days.title: Online strangers
days.work: Discuss what to do if someone online asks personal questions or to meet.

days.title: Family agreement
days.work: Write a family technology agreement with screen time, apps and rules.

days.title: Unit 4 check
days.work: Complete a quiz on fire, traffic, water, emergency and online safety.

objectives: Distinguish medicines from other drugs
Describe safe medicine use

days.title: Medicine vs. drug
days.work: Define medicine and drug and sort examples.

days.title: Labels
days.work: Read an over-the-counter medicine box for dosage, age and warnings.

days.title: Safe use
days.work: Learn the rule: take medicine only from a parent or trusted adult, never alone.

days.title: Look-alikes
days.work: Compare pictures of candy and medicine look-alikes and explain the danger.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write 5 medicine safety rules for a younger child.

objectives: Describe the harmful effects of tobacco, vaping and secondhand smoke

days.title: Effects
days.work: Compare images of healthy and smoker's lungs and list effects on the heart and lungs.

days.title: Vaping
days.work: Read a kid-level article on vaping and learn that vapes contain addictive nicotine.

days.title: Secondhand smoke
days.work: Discuss secondhand smoke and how to avoid it.

days.title: Influences
days.work: Identify how flavors, packaging and peers can make vaping seem appealing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write 5 facts about tobacco and vaping.

objectives: Describe the effects of alcohol on the body and behavior

days.title: Effects
days.work: Learn how alcohol slows the brain, affecting judgment, balance and reaction time.

days.title: Coordination
days.work: Try walking a line while spinning in place (with an adult) to model impaired balance, then discuss.

days.title: Growing bodies
days.work: Discuss why alcohol is especially harmful to growing brains and why the legal age is 21.

days.title: Influences
days.work: Identify alcohol messages in ads and media.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer 6 questions about alcohol's effects.

objectives: Demonstrate refusal skills
Encourage drug-free choices

days.title: Peer pressure
days.work: Define peer pressure and list positive and negative examples.

days.title: Refusal strategies
days.work: Learn 5 ways to say no (say no firmly, give a reason, change the subject, walk away, suggest something else).

days.title: Role-play
days.work: Role-play refusing a vape or alcohol offer in 3 scenarios.

days.title: Poster
days.work: Design a drug-free poster with a positive message for kids.

days.title: Unit 5 check
days.work: Complete a quiz on medicines, tobacco, alcohol and refusal skills.

objectives: Explain how germs spread
Practice handwashing and cough etiquette

days.title: Germs
days.work: Learn the difference between bacteria and viruses and how they spread.

days.title: Glitter germs
days.work: Put lotion and glitter 'germs' on hands, shake hands with family, and see how far they spread.

days.title: Handwashing
days.work: Practice the CDC 5-step handwashing method for 20 seconds, then test with glitter.

days.title: Cough and sneeze
days.work: Spray a water bottle 'sneeze' at paper to see droplet spread, then practice covering with an elbow.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a handwashing sign for the bathroom with all 5 steps.

objectives: Describe proper dental care
Practice brushing and flossing

days.title: Teeth
days.work: Learn tooth parts and types (incisors, canines, molars) using a mirror.

days.title: Egg experiment
days.work: Soak one hard-boiled egg in soda and one in water overnight and compare stains on the 'enamel.'

days.title: Brushing
days.work: Watch a Mouth Healthy Kids video and practice brushing for 2 minutes with a timer.

days.title: Flossing
days.work: Practice flossing technique on all teeth.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Start a 2-week brushing and flossing tracker.

objectives: Explain the importance of sleep, sun protection and personal hygiene

days.title: Sleep
days.work: Learn that 8–12-year-olds need 9–12 hours of sleep and why the brain needs it.

days.title: Sleep log
days.work: Track bedtime, wake time and hours slept for 5 nights.

days.title: Sun protection
days.work: Learn sun safety (SPF 30+, hats, shade) and test sunscreen on UV beads or dark paper in the sun.

days.title: Hygiene routine
days.work: Create a morning and evening hygiene checklist (bathing, hair, nails, clean clothes).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Analyze your sleep log and set a bedtime goal.

weeks.assessment: Sleep log analysis and hygiene checklist

objectives: Identify health care professionals and community health helpers

days.title: Helpers
days.work: List health helpers (doctor, nurse, dentist, pharmacist, school nurse, optometrist) and what each does.

days.title: Interview
days.work: Interview a health worker (in person or by phone) with 5 prepared questions.

days.title: Pharmacy
days.work: Visit a pharmacy counter and learn how pharmacists keep medicine safe.

days.title: Public health
days.work: Learn how public health workers keep water, food and restaurants safe.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a 'health helpers' booklet with one page per helper.

objectives: Describe how the environment affects health and how to protect it

days.title: Pollution
days.work: Learn how air and water pollution can affect breathing and health.

days.title: Air quality
days.work: Check the daily Air Quality Index on AirNow for a week and decide which days are good for outdoor play.

days.title: Trash audit
days.work: With gloves, sort one day of household trash into landfill, recycling and compost and weigh each.

days.title: Reduce plan
days.work: Write a family plan to reduce, reuse and recycle 3 items.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on how a clean environment keeps people healthy.

objectives: Promote a healthy community environment through action

days.title: Plan
days.work: Choose a park, beach or street to clean and plan supplies and safety rules.

days.title: Cleanup
days.work: Carry out a 1-hour cleanup with family and tally types of trash collected.

days.title: Data
days.work: Graph the trash collected and identify the most common item.

days.title: Share
days.work: Write a short letter or post for a community board sharing results and a request to help.

days.title: Unit 6 check
days.work: Complete a quiz on germs, dental care, sleep, health helpers and the environment.

objectives: Plan a health promotion campaign for a chosen audience

days.title: Topic
days.work: Choose a health topic from the year (eat a rainbow, wash hands, helmet use, drug-free) to promote.

days.title: Audience
days.work: Choose an audience (younger cousins, co-op class, family) and what they need to know.

days.title: Message
days.work: Write a clear, positive message with 3 supporting facts.

days.title: Plan materials
days.work: Plan materials: a poster, a brochure and a 1-minute public service announcement.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Share the plan with a parent and revise it.

objectives: Create accurate health promotion materials

days.title: Poster
days.work: Create a campaign poster with a catchy slogan and picture.

days.title: Brochure
days.work: Make a tri-fold brochure with facts and tips.

days.title: PSA script
days.work: Write a 1-minute PSA script.

days.title: Record
days.work: Record the PSA video or audio.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Check all facts against KidsHealth or MyPlate and practice presenting.

weeks.topic: Health promotion project: present and reflect
objectives: Present a health campaign
Reflect on health goals

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the campaign to your chosen audience.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Ask the audience what they learned and one change they will make.

days.title: Final quiz
days.work: Take the end-of-year health quiz covering all units.

days.title: Summer goals
days.work: Set 2 summer health goals (activity, nutrition, sleep or safety).

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Write a reflection on the healthiest change you made this year.
